summary: Defines a MIB extension to the GBOND-MIB module with objects for managing multi-pair bonded xDSL interfaces that use Time-Division Inverse Multiplexing, as described in the ITU-T recommendation. It is a standards-track specification.

eli5.summary: This adds more dials for bundles of phone wires where the data is split up by taking turns, so network managers can check and set them.

questions: how many services can a tdim bonded link carry
subtitle: SNMP objects for managing bundles of DSL lines that share traffic by taking turns in a fixed time frame.

tldr.problem: ITU-T G.998.3 lets several xDSL lines be bonded into one logical link carrying mixed traffic such as Ethernet, ATM and TDM, but operators had no standard SNMP objects to configure and monitor the TDIM-specific parts.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 6766 defines the G9983-MIB module, which extends the common GBOND-MIB with objects for FEC and interleaver protection, a list of up to 255 defined services of which up to 60 are active, service up and down notifications, and optional performance monitoring.
tldr.outcome: Operators can manage a G.Bond/TDIM port through SNMP, using both GBOND-MIB and G9983-MIB together. It is a Proposed Standard and has not been obsoleted.

facts.label: IANA OID in MIB-2 transmission sub-tree

today: RFC 6766 is a Proposed Standard, published in February 2013, and the unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It is meant to be used together with the GBOND-MIB of RFC 6765.

sections.title: What G.Bond/TDIM Is and What This MIB Covers
sections.content:
Multi-pair bonding using Time-Division Inverse Multiplexing (TDIM), also called G.Bond/TDIM, is specified in ITU-T Recommendation G.998.3. It bonds (aggregates) multiple xDSL lines, or individual bearer channels in multiple xDSL lines, into a single bidirectional logical link. That link can carry a mix of traffic streams such as Ethernet, Asynchronous Transfer Mode (ATM) and Time-Division Multiplexing (TDM).

RFC 6766 defines a Management Information Base (MIB) module, G9983-MIB, with objects specific to G.Bond/TDIM. It extends the common bonding objects of the GBOND-MIB module from RFC 6765. The module follows the SMIv2 rules and is meant to be accessed through SNMP.
sections.eli5: Several phone wires can be joined to act like one fat wire. This memo is a list of settings and meters for managing that fat wire when its pieces take turns sending.

sections.title: Relationship to Other MIB Modules
sections.content:
A G.Bond/TDIM port is a special case of a bonded multi-pair xDSL interface. It is managed with the generic interface objects of the IF-MIB from RFC 2863, and an interface index (ifIndex) identifies both G.Bond/TDIM ports and the individual xDSL lines and channels.

The GBOND-MIB from RFC 6765 holds the objects common to all bonded multi-pair xDSL interfaces, such as bonding management, port and channel configuration and the initialization sequence. Both the GBOND-MIB and G9983-MIB modules are REQUIRED to manage a G.Bond/TDIM port.

The document also builds on the Broadband Forum report TR-159, which defines a management model and a hierarchy of managed objects for bonded xDSL interfaces. A table in the RFC maps TR-159 attributes to the SNMP objects defined here, and all objects defined in G.998.3 have corresponding TR-159 objects.
sections.eli5: This memo is an add-on pack. You need the main rulebook (the GBOND-MIB) and this add-on together to manage a TDIM bundle.

sections.title: Structure of the G9983-MIB Module
sections.content:
All objects live under a single group, g9983Port, split into six sub-groups following the guidelines of RFC 4181:

  • g9983PortNotifications holds the service down and up notifications.
  • g9983PortConfTable holds configuration objects for a port.
  • g9983PortCapTable holds objects reflecting the port's capabilities.
  • g9983PortStatTable holds overall status, complementing the ifTable and the gBondPortStatFltStatus object of GBOND-MIB.
  • g9983SvcTable holds configuration and status of services.
  • g9983PM holds objects for optional historical performance monitoring.

Link protection is configured in the configuration table. G.Bond/TDIM allows an optional Forward Error Correction (FEC) and interleaver block, which, when supported and enabled, gives some protection against micro-interruptions, alien noise and even failure of an individual Bonding Channel Entity (BCE), also called cut-line protection.
sections.eli5: The settings are sorted into six labelled drawers: alerts, settings, what the gear can do, current status, the list of jobs, and score keeping.

sections.title: Services and Drop Priority
sections.content:
Unlike the other two xDSL bonding schemes (G.Bond/ATM and G.Bond/Ethernet), which send the information needed to reassemble fragmented data along with the data, G.Bond/TDIM is a synchronous scheme. Both ends must know the data distribution tables before any data can flow. Service changes are announced through Bonding Communication Channel (BCC) messages, which switch both ends to the new configuration together, so services can be configured whether the link is in service or not.

Up to 60 services can be active on a link. The MIB lets a manager define up to 255 services in g9983SvcTable, then choose the active ones with g9983PortConfAdminServices, a byte-vector of service indices listed in their order in the G.Bond/TDIM frame. The read-only g9983OperSvcTable shows the actual list, indexed from 1 by position, so a manager can walk it with GET-NEXT. Service configuration can only be changed on the Bonding Terminating Unit at the Central Office (BTU-C). The sum of all services' bandwidth SHOULD be less than or equal to the target data rate, and G.Bond/TDIM links are symmetrical.

When bandwidth degrades, lower-priority services are impaired or dropped first. Synchronous services (fractional DS1/E1, clear channel E1/T1, T3/E3, clock) placed early in the frame outrank asynchronous ones (Ethernet, ATM, GFP-encapsulated) placed farther along. Among services of the same type, a lower position means higher priority.

A higher-priority service can be dropped before a lower-priority one. In the RFC's example, a 2-Mbps link carries a T1 service of 1.5 Mbps at position 1 and an Ethernet service of 0.5 Mbps at position 2. When the link falls to 1.4 Mbps, the T1 service is dropped and the Ethernet service stays up.
sections.eli5: It is like packing a lunchbox in order of importance. If the box shrinks, the things at the back are the first to be left out, unless the thing at the front simply does not fit.

sections.title: Notifications and Performance Monitoring
sections.content:
The module provides g9983SvcUp and g9983SvcDown notifications for each configured service. During degradation several services may be suspended at once, according to their drop priority. Notifications SHOULD be rate-limited so that there is an implementation-specific gap between consecutive notifications of the same event, which prevents flooding when g9983OperSvcState flips between up and down. Rate-limited notifications are dropped, not queued for later.

The optional performance monitoring counters, thresholds and history buckets are similar to those of TR-159 and use the 64-bit textual conventions of the HC-PerfHist-TC-MIB from RFC 3705. The agent SHOULD align each interval with a fifteen-minute boundary of the wall clock, and each one-day interval with the start of a day. Counters are not reset when the port is re-initialized, only when the agent is reset or re-initialized. Counting of some events is inhibited during periods of service unavailability, as each counter's DESCRIPTION clause states.
sections.eli5: The gear can ring a bell when a job stops or restarts, but it will not ring over and over. It also keeps score in 15-minute rounds.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
Writable objects can hurt if unprotected. Changing g9983PortConfAdminServices can disrupt service by moving a service (changing its drop priority) or removing it. Changing g9983SvcTable parameters such as g9983SvcType or g9983SvcSize can impair a service, for example dropping a TDM service when bandwidth is short. Changing g9983PortConfTable parameters such as g9983PortConfFecAdminState can degrade link quality and rate or even cause link initialization to fail.

Readable objects can also be sensitive. Because the pairs of a bonded port may share a bundle with pairs belonging to another operator or customer, the RFC notes it is theoretically possible to eavesdrop on a G.Bond transmission by listening to cross-talk, especially if the link's operating parameters are known. Objects such as g9983PortStatFecOperState and the g9983OperSvcTable could aid that, so even GET and NOTIFY access should be controlled.

Implementations SHOULD provide the SNMPv3 security features. Those claiming SNMPv3 compliance MUST fully support authentication and privacy through the User-based Security Model with AES. Deploying SNMP versions before SNMPv3 is NOT RECOMMENDED.
sections.eli5: If a stranger can flip the switches, the connection can break, and if a stranger can read the meters, they may learn how to snoop. So only trusted people should get access, with a secret handshake.
